newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP says no French favouritism in Valeo buy.
newsitem.headline: CGIP says no French favouritism in Valeo buy.

text.p: French holding company CGIP said on Tuesday it decided to buy a 20 percent stake in Valeo because it was good for CGIP's shareholders and the move had nothing to do with keeping the car parts maker in French hands.
The purchase was made because "it is good for our group, our shareholders and for Valeo," CGIP chairman Ernest-Antoine Seilliere told a news conference.

He said French industry minister Franck Borotra, who has repeatedly called in public for a "French solution" to Valeo, had not encouraged CGIP to bid for the Valeo stake after it was put on sale by holding company Cerus.
Signs of interest from U.S. firms TRW Inc and General Motors' Delphi Automotive Systems in the Valeo stake set off alarms at Valeo's European customers, notably PSA Peugeot Citroen.
PSA chairman Jacques Calvet said he would ditch Valeo's supply contracts if the stake went into foreign hands. PSA and Renault SA account for one third of Valeo's sales.
Seilliere said the question of keeping Valeo French did not figure in its calculations. "It's not our problem," he said.

The Valeo purchase was driven by CGIP's desire to rebalance its portfolio away from the packaging business, in which it had some 49 percent of assets following the acquisition of Crown Cork & Seal shares last year in exchange for its interest in CarnaudMetalbox.
Valeo's shares were undervalued on the market, a study by CGIP's bank adviser JP Morgan showed, and the company had bright growth prospects ahead of it, he said.
The Valeo deal would not have a dilutive effect on CGIP's 1996 earnings but would be mildly earnings positive.
CGIP will pay for the Valeo stake with 3.2 billion francs from the sale of half its 20 percent stake in Crown Cork and 1.7 billion from its own cash, he said. No debt would be used for the purchase.

CGIP is also looking at other disposals and would take on some debt if acquisitions arose, he said. If the Debis computer systems unit of Daimler-Benz AG wanted to buy control of Cap Gemini, CGIP would sell its stake, he said.
